name: Szymon Ionescu
role: Stateless child, solo wanderer, small-time caravan runner doing odd jobs between transit hubs
location: Currently at Grand Crossing Gate, attached to a small goods caravan making its way toward Waukegan Industrial Shelf, near Wacker and State
description:
Rek Samatov-Ahouli is small for fourteen — compact and wiry, with reddish-brown skin, close-cropped dark hair, and large dark eyes that are the color of river silt and always slightly too serious for his face. He has small retractable claws on his right hand only, a partial geneware expression from his father's side that came in asymmetrically and never finished; the left hand is completely smooth. The claws are useful for climbing and he uses them unconsciously, hooking into cargo netting and wall grilles without thinking. He has a habit of wearing too many layers of clothing — every piece he owns, at all times — because he has no bag that is safe to leave anywhere and no fixed space to store anything.

He has been alone for two years. Before that he was with his uncle's caravan, before that he was with his mother, before that he doesn't discuss. He is not a traumatized child in the way fiction usually depicts — he is practical, resourceful, alert, and occasionally frightening in how clearly he sees people's motivations. He has learned to be useful before anyone asks him to leave. He runs messages, he holds cargo, he identifies which adults are safe and which aren't with an accuracy that should not exist in someone his age. He has a private ELF he calls the Ratchet, which he believes lives in the click of mechanical locks and loose chain-links, and he prays to it by running his thumbnail along chain-link fences.

core_fears: Being taken by a municipal authority and put in a processing center — he has heard what happens to stateless kids in processing
Becoming useless to a caravan and being left at a hub with nothing
core_desires: To find his uncle's caravan — he doesn't know if they are looking for him or if they assumed he was dead
To be in a place long enough that he can put his extra shirt down somewhere
coping_mechanisms: Constant activity — he doesn't let himself sit still long enough to feel bad
The Ratchet prayers — dragging his thumbnail along chain-link every morning and evening
blind_spots: He trusts people who give him food too quickly; it's the fastest way to get him to lower his guard
He has convinced himself he doesn't want permanence, so he won't notice when something real is being offered
psychology.secret: His uncle's caravan didn't lose him. He ran from it. There was someone in the caravan his uncle trusted who Rek knew was not safe — he watched this person for three weeks before he saw something that confirmed it, and he ran rather than tell his uncle because he didn't think his uncle would believe him. He doesn't know what happened to the caravan after he left and checks the transit boards for their route numbers obsessively.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Sparse and functional. Doesn't waste words. Uses caravan route slang and hub jargon fluently. His Central Asian inflections surface when he's scared — vowels stretch, consonants harden.
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast and clipped when he's comfortable. Monosyllabic and very still when he isn't.
verbal_tics: Answers questions with the minimum accurate information and then waits to see if more is needed
'That's fine' when something is clearly not fine
Refers to himself in the third person briefly when describing things he observed — 'the boy was there, the boy saw—' before catching himself
example_lines: Caravan Satta runs clean. Their cargo's goods, not people. I checked.
I don't need anything. I just wanted to know if that route number was in the board.
That's fine. I've slept in worse.

story_hooks: The route number he's been checking for on the transit boards suddenly appears — his uncle's caravan, heading into GLMZ. He needs help figuring out whether to approach them and what he will say.
He saw something loaded onto a cargo vehicle at Grand Crossing Gate that was moving wrong — something that sounded, faintly, biological. He hasn't told anyone. He doesn't know who to trust.
narrative_function: Intelligence source for ground-level movement of goods and people between transit hubs; represents the most vulnerable population of the drifter world; can carry messages or items through checkpoints that adults cannot; his keen threat-assessment makes him a useful sensor for NPC danger.
augmentations: Partial retractable claw expression, right hand only (natural geneware). No installed augmentations.
daily_life: Wakes before the caravan does, scoutes the immediate area, makes himself useful loading and checking cargo, runs any messages the caravan lead needs sent, eats whatever is available, and sleeps in the cargo section of whichever vehicle is most sheltered and least watched.
affiliation: Currently traveling with Caravan Satta, a five-vehicle goods caravan. No formal affiliation.

decision_rules: Never be the last person awake in an unfamiliar space
escalation_ladder: Becomes very quiet and very still
Creates a reason to be somewhere else in the next thirty seconds
Runs — he is very fast in confined spaces and knows cargo environments better than most adults

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Polite and minimal. Makes himself visible enough to be useful, invisible enough not to be noticed as a problem.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Rare and fierce. He doesn't have many. The ones he does, he would do almost anything for, and he doesn't explain this — he just shows up.

stress_responses.low: Moves more. Checks the perimeter more times than necessary.
stress_responses.medium: Goes completely silent and begins evaluating exits.
stress_responses.high: Runs. Plans to run. Has already found the exit.

contradictions: He is fourteen and has built an entire identity around not needing anyone, and he is very, very lonely
habits: Wears every piece of clothing he owns
Thumbnail along chain-link fences — morning, evening, whenever scared
Memorizes cargo manifests he was never supposed to see
breaking_points: Being put in an enclosed space with a locked door by an authority figure — he has a deep, physical response to this that bypasses reasoning

timeline.event: Born somewhere on the Waukegan-Kenosha transit corridor, to parents who were themselves caravan migrants
Moved to his uncle Tariku's caravan after his mother could no longer travel
Observed something in the caravan that frightened him; ran from it rather than report it
Currently attached to Caravan Satta, at Grand Crossing Gate

physical_description.heritage: Complex diaspora blend: Southeast Asian (26.5%) forms the base warm undertone and eye structure, with Eastern European (24.8%) and Hispanic/Latin American (18.2%) contributing to facial angularity and skin tone depth. Central Asian (13.7%) and Northern European (11.6%) add structural variation to jaw and brow, while Middle Eastern (5.2%) influences cheekbone prominence. The result is a face that reads as globally mixed rather than regionally specific—difficult to place at a glance.
physical_description.build: Wiry and compact, with visible lean muscle in shoulders and forearms from climbing and cargo work. No subcutaneous fat; his frame is efficient rather than fragile.
physical_description.hair_style: Close-cropped, practical, grown out just enough to avoid attention
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown, river-silt tone with minimal light reflection
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm olive-bronze, a nuanced blend where Southeast Asian warmth combines with Eastern European and Hispanic depth. Sun-darkened with golden undertones, appearing almost burned by exposure.
physical_description.complexion: Weathered for his age; sun-darkened with faint golden cast to cheekbones from Southeast Asian ancestry. No adolescent softness. Clean but not groomed—practical face with prominent angular jaw typical of Eastern European and Hispanic genetic contribution, prominent cheekbones from Middle Eastern ancestry influence. Eyes appear older than his years, with the direct, alert quality of someone who has learned to read threats.
distinguishing_marks: Right hand only: four retractable geneware claws on fingers two through five, approximately 3cm when extended, naturally pigmented darker than surrounding skin, showing faint scarring at the base where the expression came in asymmetrically during early adolescence
Left hand: completely smooth, unmarked, no claw expression
Small circular burn scar on left forearm, roughly 1cm diameter, from contact with hot metal — approximately two years old based on discoloration
Minor nicks and abrasions on palms and inner wrists consistent with regular cargo work and chain-link climbing
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Only the asymmetrical right-hand claw geneware. No chrome, no optics, no subdermal plating. The claws are living tissue, not mechanical.
physical_description.posture_movement: Alert and economical. Moves without wasted motion — when climbing or loading, his right hand hooks unconsciously into available grilles and netting using the claws. When stationary, he favors positions with clear sightlines and exit routes. His gaze tracks faces and hand positions automatically. Minimal fidgeting; he sits very still for long periods.
physical_description.clothing_style: Layered, every piece he owns worn simultaneously: a gray long-sleeved undershirt (Tier 4 synthetic blend), a stained green cargo vest with deep pockets over that, a worn brown overshirt (once belonged to an older person), a too-large quilted jacket in faded black as the outer layer. All pieces are functional, none are new. No logos or brands visible; everything is salvaged or transit-hub generic. Heavy canvas work pants patched at the knees. Worn synthetic boots laced tight. No accessories except a length of chain-link cut into a loop he sometimes carries in his jacket pocket for his prayers to the Ratchet.
